[`assertions.svh`](include/common_cells/assertions.svh) contains macros that expand to assertion blocks.\n166: These macros should recduce the effort in writing many assertions and make it\n167: easier to use them. They are similar to but incompatible with the macros used by [lowrisc](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/master/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_assert.sv).\n168: \n169: #### Simple Assertion and Cover Macros\n170: | Macro              | Arguments                                        | Description                                                                |\n171: | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n172: | <code>`ASSERT_I</code>     | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Immediate assertion                                                        |\n173: | <code>`ASSERT_INIT</code>  | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in initial block. Can be used for things like parameter checking |\n174: | <code>`ASSERT_FINAL</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assertion in final block                                                   |\n175: | <code>`ASSERT</code>       | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property directly                                      |\n176: | <code>`ASSERT_NEVER</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assert a concurrent property NEVER happens                                 |\n177: | <code>`ASSERT_KNOWN</code> | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)  | Concurrent clocked assertion with custom error message                     |\n178: | <code>`COVER</code>        | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`)           | Cover a concurrent property                                                |\n179: - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*\n180: - *`__desc` is an optional string argument describing the failure causing the assertion to be violated that is embedded into the error report and defaults to `\"\"`.*\n181: \n182: #### Complex Assertion Macros\n183: | Macro                 | Arguments                                                                           | Description                                                                                                |\n184: | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n185: | <code>`ASSERT_PULSE</code>    | `__name`, `__sig`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                                     | Assert that signal is an active-high pulse with pulse length of 1 clock cycle                              |\n186: | <code>`ASSERT_IF</code>       | `__name`, `__prop`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                        | Assert that a property is true only when an enable signal is set                                           |\n187: | <code>`ASSERT_KNOWN_IF</code> | `__name`, `__sig`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)                         | Assert that signal has a known value (each bit is either '0' or '1') after reset if enable is set          |\n188: | <code>`ASSERT_STABLE</code>   | `__name`, `__valid`, `__ready`, `__data`, `__enable`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`)  | Assert that the data on a ready-valid interface is kept stable after valid is asserted, until ready is too |\n189: - *The name of the clock and reset signals for implicit variants is `clk_i` and `rst_ni`, respectively.*\n190: - *`__desc` is an optional string argument describing the failure causing the assertion to be violated that is embedded into the error report and defaults to `\"\"`.*\n191: \n192: #### Assumption Macros\n193: \n194: | Macro          | Arguments                                        | Description                  |\n195: | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |\n196: | <code>`ASSUME</code>   | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__clk`, `__rst`, `__desc`) | Assume a concurrent property |\n197: | <code>`ASSUME_I</code> | `__name`, `__prop`, (`__desc`)                   | Assume an immediate property |\n198: -
